note: Theropod run: duty below half, so there is a moment with no foot down at all. The body pitches forward over the hips and the tail comes up level behind it as the counterweight that makes that pitch possible -- a two-legged runner that keeps its tail down falls over. Wings clamp in tight; this is a ground gait, not a take-off. The crouch is deep because it has to be: a hind leg only reaches 0.16 past its rest length, and lowering the hip is what buys the stride enough room to land.
